risks.title: Legacy PLC/SCADA integration complexity
risks.description: Older PLCs and SCADA systems use obsolete or undocumented protocols and lack native connectivity, making data extraction and control integration slow and error-prone.
early_warning_signals: Missing or partial register/tag maps during discovery
Vendor unable to provide protocol documentation
Protocol bridging tests stall beyond estimates
risks.mitigation: Complete thorough protocol capture in Phase 1; engage OEMs early; budget contingency time for reverse-engineering tags; prefer edge gateways with broad protocol libraries.
risks.contingency: Fall back to sensor-based or I/O-level data acquisition where protocol access is impossible; phase the line in once documentation is obtained.

risks.title: Proprietary protocol lock-in
risks.description: Reliance on vendor-proprietary protocols or closed data formats limits interoperability and increases switching costs across the technology stack.
early_warning_signals: Vendors refuse OPC UA or open API access
Data available only through paid connectors
Custom connectors required for each system
risks.mitigation: Mandate open protocols (OPC UA, MQTT/Sparkplug B) and documented APIs in RFPs; normalize data at the edge; avoid storing proprietary formats in the lake.
risks.contingency: Introduce a middleware abstraction layer to insulate the platform from proprietary dependencies.

risks.title: Production disruption from OT changes
risks.description: Network, gateway, or sensor installation on running lines risks unplanned downtime, scrap, or safety events during deployment.
early_warning_signals: Limited shutdown windows in the plan
risks.mitigation: Restrict changes to approved production windows; stage and dry-run in a non-production cell; use read-only connections first; pair with OT technicians.
risks.contingency: Maintain rapid rollback procedures and pre-positioned spares; halt deployment if any quality or safety metric moves out of band.

risks.title: Time synchronization issues across devices
risks.description: Inconsistent timestamps across PLCs, gateways, edge, and platform corrupt event correlation, traceability, and root-cause analysis.
risks.mitigation: Deploy PTP grandmaster with NTP fallback; enforce time-sync on all devices; validate drift during commissioning.
risks.contingency: Apply time-correction logic in the context layer for known drift; recalibrate clocks before resuming analytics.

risks.title: Brownfield vs greenfield complexity
risks.description: Brownfield environments impose constraints (legacy equipment, limited space, hazardous areas) that inflate effort versus greenfield assumptions.
early_warning_signals: Discovery revealing more legacy assets than expected
risks.mitigation: Run explicit brownfield constraints analysis in Phase 1; budget brownfield-specific effort and environmental-rated hardware.
risks.contingency: Sequence brownfield lines last; deploy via non-invasive sensors where modifications are infeasible.

risks.title: Multi-vendor equipment incompatibility
risks.description: Equipment from multiple vendors with differing ages, protocols, and data models complicates consistent integration and normalization.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the ISA-95 data model and tag naming convention; normalize at the edge; maintain a canonical tag dictionary.
risks.contingency: Add a vendor-specific adaptation layer per equipment family until normalization is complete.

risks.title: Sequence-of-operations disruption
risks.description: Instrumentation or control changes may interfere with the established sequence of operations, causing cycle-time or quality regressions.
risks.mitigation: Map sequence of operations in Phase 1; validate non-interference in a test cell; monitor cycle time and quality post-change.
risks.contingency: Revert changes and re-baseline the sequence before retrying with modified approach.

risks.title: HMI/SCADA upgrade conflicts
risks.description: Planned or vendor-driven HMI/SCADA upgrades may conflict with new integrations, breaking tag mappings or displays.
early_warning_signals: Loss of OPC endpoints after upgrades
risks.mitigation: Coordinate upgrade roadmaps with the program; freeze tag mappings during integration testing; version-control interface definitions.
risks.contingency: Roll back upgrades or re-establish integrations through documented migration steps.

risks.title: OT network exposure during IT/OT convergence
risks.description: Connecting previously isolated OT networks to enterprise/cloud expands the attack surface and can expose control systems to IT-borne threats.
risks.mitigation: Implement IEC 62443 zones/conduits and deny-by-default DMZ; validate segmentation before enabling new paths; baseline OT traffic.
risks.contingency: Temporarily disconnect new conduits and quarantine affected zones if an intrusion is suspected.

risks.title: Ransomware impacting production
risks.description: Ransomware spreading from IT into OT could halt production, damage equipment, and cause extended downtime and revenue loss.
risks.mitigation: Segment OT from IT; deploy OT-aware monitoring/IDS; immutable backups; tested incident response and tabletop exercises.
risks.contingency: Invoke OT incident response plan; isolate zones; restore from known-good backups; engage IR retainer.

risks.title: Insecure remote access for vendors
risks.description: Vendor and support remote access, if uncontrolled, creates a persistent pathway into OT for attackers.
risks.mitigation: Mandate jump-host + MFA + session recording for all remote access; time-bound approvals; remove legacy modems.
risks.contingency: Revoke access immediately and rotate credentials upon any suspicious session.

risks.title: Unauthorized control system access
risks.description: Weak access controls could allow unauthorized users to alter controller logic or setpoints, risking safety and quality.
risks.mitigation: Enforce RBAC and least privilege; strong authentication for engineering access; change control for logic/setpoint changes.
risks.contingency: Revoke access, revert unauthorized changes, and forensic-review the affected controllers.

risks.title: Insecure protocol usage on converged network
risks.description: Unencrypted legacy protocols (e.g., plain Modbus, OPC DA) carried across the converged network expose data and enable spoofing/replay.
risks.mitigation: Terminate legacy protocols at the edge; use OPC UA with security and mutual TLS for northbound traffic; encrypt inter-zone conduits.
risks.contingency: Restrict legacy protocols to isolated conduits with strict firewall rules pending upgrade.

risks.title: Vulnerability in edge/IoT devices
risks.description: Edge gateways, sensors, and cameras may ship with vulnerabilities, weak defaults, or limited patching support.
risks.mitigation: Require vendor vulnerability disclosure and patch SLAs in procurement; harden configs; isolate devices within zones.
risks.contingency: Quarantine vulnerable devices and apply compensating controls (segmentation, monitoring) until patched or replaced.

risks.title: Lack of OT patching cadence
risks.description: OT systems are rarely patched due to uptime requirements, leaving known vulnerabilities exploitable over time.
risks.mitigation: Define a risk-based OT patching cadence aligned to maintenance windows; virtual patching via IPS; track patch compliance as a KPI.
risks.contingency: Apply virtual patches and tighten segmentation for high-risk vulnerabilities until formal patching is possible.

risks.title: Insufficient incident response for OT
risks.description: Incident response processes built for IT may not account for OT safety and uptime constraints, delaying safe containment.
early_warning_signals: Unclear authority to isolate OT zones
Tabletop exercises failing on OT scenarios
risks.mitigation: Develop OT-specific IR playbooks with operations and safety; define containment authority; run regular tabletops.
risks.contingency: Engage specialized OT IR retainer and follow pre-approved containment steps during an incident.

risks.title: Poor data quality from floor devices
risks.description: Noisy, miscalibrated, or missing readings from floor devices undermine analytics, dashboards, and model accuracy.
risks.mitigation: Enforce calibration; instrument data quality rules and steward workflows; validate sensors against references during commissioning.
risks.contingency: Quarantine low-quality tags from analytics and re-instrument or recalibrate before re-enabling.

risks.title: Time-series data gaps due to network latency
risks.description: Network latency, jitter, or link interruptions can create gaps in time-series data that corrupt analytics and OEE calculations.
risks.mitigation: Engineer network for deterministic performance where needed; use edge buffering with store-and-forward; monitor completeness.
risks.contingency: Backfill from edge buffers and flag affected intervals as low-confidence in analytics.

risks.title: Data labeling quality for vision models
risks.description: Inconsistent or inaccurate labels for vision datasets (e.g., micro-crack vs. scratch) degrade model precision and recall.
early_warning_signals: Low model confidence on validation set
risks.mitigation: Define a clear defect taxonomy; use trained annotators with QA sampling; consensus labeling and review loops.
risks.contingency: Pause training, relabel the affected dataset, and re-validate before redeployment.

risks.title: Model drift over production changes
risks.description: Process, material, or product changes cause production data to drift from training distributions, degrading model performance over time.
risks.mitigation: Monitor data and model drift; schedule retraining; gate production updates on validation; track change events.
risks.contingency: Roll back to last validated model or fall back to rule-based/safe-state until retrained.

risks.title: Data silos between MES/ERP/SCADA
risks.description: Data trapped in MES, ERP, and SCADA silos prevents end-to-end visibility and traceability across the value stream.
early_warning_signals: Manual data exports still in use
risks.mitigation: Build governed integrations and a shared context layer; reconcile master data across systems.
risks.contingency: Use interim ETL snapshots to bridge silos while integrations are completed.

risks.title: Insufficient historical data for ML training
risks.description: Limited or low-fidelity historical data may be inadequate to train reliable predictive and analytics models.
risks.mitigation: Start data collection early; augment with physics-based or synthetic data; prioritize models feasible with available data.
risks.contingency: Defer advanced models until sufficient data accrues; deliver rule-based analytics in the interim.

risks.title: Data governance not enforced
risks.description: Without enforced governance, data ownership, quality, and access controls erode, reducing trust and creating compliance exposure.
risks.mitigation: Stand up data governance with stewards, quality rules, and access controls from Phase 2; audit periodically.
risks.contingency: Quarantine ungoverned datasets and assign temporary stewards pending ownership decisions.

risks.title: Vendor lock-in for historian/MES platform
risks.description: Choosing a historian or MES platform with proprietary formats and connectors can lock the client in and raise long-term costs.
risks.mitigation: Prefer platforms with open APIs/standards; negotiate data portability and exit clauses; keep a canonical open-format copy.
risks.contingency: Maintain an open-format mirror to enable migration if lock-in costs escalate.

risks.title: Edge hardware failure in factory environment
risks.description: Edge compute and gateways exposed to heat, dust, vibration, and power issues may fail more often than rated, impacting availability.
risks.mitigation: Select ruggedized, environmentally rated hardware; proper cooling/UPS; redundancy on critical edge nodes; spare stock.
risks.contingency: Fail over to redundant nodes and replace failed units from spares; derate workloads if environmental limits are near.

risks.title: Cloud connectivity dependency
risks.description: Reliance on cloud for analytics or training creates a dependency on connectivity; outages can degrade insights and some control functions.
risks.mitigation: Keep critical/low-latency workloads on edge with local fallback; buffer and store-and-forward; design for intermittent connectivity.
risks.contingency: Switch to edge-only mode for critical functions and queue data for cloud until connectivity restores.

risks.title: Open-source tool maintainability
risks.description: Open-source components may lack vendor support, creating maintenance and security burden over time if not governed.
risks.mitigation: Prefer projects with active communities or commercial support; document support model; track OSS inventory and CVEs.
risks.contingency: Engage commercial support or migrate to supported equivalents for critical unsupported components.

risks.title: Software license cost escalation
risks.description: Tag-based, core-based, or consumption-based licensing can escalate sharply as the rollout scales to more lines and assets.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate scaling tiers and caps upfront; model full-plant license economics; rationalize tags and users before licensing.
risks.contingency: Switch metering model or vendor for non-differentiating components if costs breach thresholds.

risks.title: Long lead times for industrial hardware
risks.description: Industrial hardware (gateways, ruggedized servers, cameras) can have long lead times and customs delays that slip deployment windows.
early_warning_signals: Staging not ready for deployment wave
risks.mitigation: Order early; plan logistics/customs in Phase 3; hold buffer stock; qualify alternate vendors/skus.
risks.contingency: Re-sequence deployment waves around available hardware and source alternates for critical items.

risks.title: Pilot fails to demonstrate ROI
risks.description: If the 90-day pilot does not show measurable yield/OEE gains, funding and stakeholder confidence for scaling may be withdrawn.
risks.mitigation: Select a representative, high-impact line; baseline carefully; instrument first; track value weekly and course-correct.
risks.contingency: Pivot the pilot scope to a higher-value use case and extend by a defined window before a go/no-go decision.

risks.title: Scope creep from operations team
risks.description: Operations stakeholders may add requirements and use cases mid-program, diluting focus and stretching timelines and budget.
risks.mitigation: Enforce a change control process; park new asks in a backlog; tie scope to ROI and phase plan.
risks.contingency: Defer approved changes to later waves; reset baseline if material changes are approved.

risks.title: Plant commissioning delays impacting deployment windows
risks.description: New line commissioning or maintenance turnarounds may consume production windows, pushing deployment windows out.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate deployment windows with plant scheduling early; maintain a flexible wave plan; pre-stage to compress field time.
risks.contingency: Shift affected work to alternate lines/windows and re-baseline the schedule.

risks.title: Change resistance from shop-floor operators
risks.description: Operators may resist new dashboards, alerts, or AI-influenced workflows, undermining adoption and value realization.
risks.mitigation: Involve operators early; co-design workflows; deliver training and quick wins; show how tools reduce their burden.
risks.contingency: Launch a focused adoption push with super-users and simplify workflows based on operator feedback.

risks.title: Skill shortage for OT/data roles
risks.description: Scarce talent at the intersection of OT, data, and cybersecurity can slow delivery and inflate costs.
risks.mitigation: Combine partner staff with internal upskilling; cross-train; document knowledge; build a reskilling roadmap.
risks.contingency: Engage managed services/partners to bridge gaps and re-pace non-critical workstreams.

risks.title: Phase 0 diagnostic underestimates complexity
risks.description: An optimistic diagnostic may underestimate brownfield complexity, integration depth, and skill needs, leading to under-budgeting.
risks.mitigation: Ground the diagnostic in on-site assessment; use ranges not point estimates; carry management reserve.
risks.contingency: Re-baseline scope, budget, and timeline with the steering committee; phase scope to fit the envelope.

risks.title: Funding discontinuity between phases
risks.description: Stage-gated funding may pause or stop between phases, causing team attrition and loss of momentum.
risks.mitigation: Show value at each gate; pre-secure multi-phase funding; maintain a benefits tracker to justify continuation.
risks.contingency: Scale back to a maintenance footprint on delivered value while securing renewed funding.

risks.title: Budget overrun on Phase 4-5
risks.description: Network, edge, and platform build phases typically consume the most capital and are prone to overruns from integration and rework.
risks.mitigation: Front-load discovery and design rigor; fixed-price components where feasible; track EV and forecast weekly.
risks.contingency: Re-prioritize scope within the phase envelope; defer non-critical scope to later waves.

risks.title: Unclear decision rights for OT/IT governance
risks.description: Ambiguity between corporate IT, plant OT, and the digital team over who decides slows approvals and creates conflicts.
early_warning_signals: Conflicting directives from IT and OT
risks.mitigation: Define a clear decision-rights matrix and a joint IT/OT change advisory board with executive sponsorship.
risks.contingency: Escalate to the steering committee for binding decisions and update the rights matrix.

risks.title: Vendor SOW gaps leading to change orders
risks.description: Loosely scoped SOWs with system integrators and vendors generate change orders that inflate cost and delay delivery.
risks.mitigation: Write precise SOWs tied to deliverables and acceptance criteria; align scope to architecture; include assumptions and exclusions.
risks.contingency: Negotiate change orders against a priced change framework; re-baseline the vendor plan if material.

risks.title: Contract dispute on data ownership
risks.description: Ambiguity over ownership and usage rights of generated data and models can lead to disputes with vendors and integrators.
early_warning_signals: Vendors claiming rights to derived assets
risks.mitigation: Explicitly assign ownership of data, derived data, and models to the client in all contracts; define vendor usage rights.
risks.contingency: Renegotiate affected clauses and restrict vendor access until ownership is clarified.

risks.title: IP protection for custom ML models
risks.description: Custom ML models and analytics represent valuable IP that may be exposed or co-opted without clear protection terms.
early_warning_signals: Models hosted on vendor infrastructure without IP terms
risks.mitigation: Assert IP ownership and confidentiality for custom models; control model artifacts and registries; restrict reuse rights.
risks.contingency: Migrate model assets under client control and enforce confidentiality/ownership through legal review.
